builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding
summary: The method replaces single-token autoregressive decoding with parallel generation of mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass, trained via a variational objective combining autoregressive and parallel decoding losses. It requires pretraining the model with this objective from scratch, so it cannot be applied to existing pretrained checkpoints, and the reported speedups depend on latent-variable routing that adds training and inference complexity. Failure modes include quality degradation on tasks where token dependencies are poorly captured by the latent variables, and the power-law speedup claim is validated only up to 3B parameters, leaving behavior at production model scales unverified.
rationale: The approach requires foundation-model pretraining with a custom objective, which exceeds the reader's infrastructure, and no off-the-shelf pretrained PLM checkpoints compatible with standard APIs currently exist, so it is relevant to monitor but not adoptable now.
technique: Parallel token decoding via variational latent variables

claims.statement: The method replaces single-token autoregressive decoding with parallel generation of mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass, trained via a variational objective combining autoregressive and parallel decoding losses. It requires pretraining the model with this objective from scratch, so it cannot be applied to existing pretrained checkpoints, and the reported speedups depend on latent-variable routing that adds training and inference complexity. Failure modes include quality degradation on tasks where token dependencies are poorly captured by the latent variables, and the power-law speedup claim is validated only up to 3B parameters, leaving behavior at production model scales unverified.

A post-trained 1.3B PLM matches or exceeds an identically trained autoregressive model on math, coding, and instruction-following benchmarks with 2.3-5.7x inference speedup; speedup follows a power law in model size across 80M-3B scales.
